dossier.summary: Kessler Foods makes frozen meals and sauces for grocery private labels at two plants in Ohio, and ships to regional distribution centers through outside carriers.
dossier.why_now: Announced a third plant in Indiana, due to open in 2027.

data.booth_note: Two of us at the stand the whole show, the dispatch board running live on the big screen, and a quiet corner at the back with chairs and decent coffee.

booth_hours.who: Maya Lindqvist from 11:00 am, Jonas Petrov all day

talk.title: What a new plant does to your carrier mix, and how to plan it a year out
talk.speaker: Jonas Petrov, Lanternline

side_events.title: Opening night drinks
side_events.note: Most of the exhibitors go. The easy place to find us if Tuesday is your only day.

side_events.title: Breakfast for food and beverage operations leaders
side_events.note: Twenty people, one table, no slides. Ask Maya for a seat.

side_events.title: Shippers and carriers dinner
side_events.where: Off site, a ten minute walk from the hall
side_events.note: Invite only. We have two spare seats at our table.

side_events.title: Closing panel on the next twelve months in freight
side_events.note: The one session worth staying for on the last day.

data.why_now: Announced a third plant in Indiana, due to open in 2027.
data.personal_line: A third plant in Indiana means new lanes and new carriers to set up before it opens, and that is the exact problem the board on our stand is built around. Twenty minutes is enough to see whether it fits how Kessler runs the Ohio plants today.
